finding.claim: Xxh32::update's fast-path check compares a u32-truncated input length against the 16-byte buffer, but the subsequent copy uses the full usize length, so a single slice of 4 GiB or more with length congruent to k mod 2^32 (k < 16) overflows the inline mem buffer in release builds.
finding.source: Length and contents of one byte slice passed to Xxh32::update or Xxh32::write (src/xxh32.rs:200-201) on a 64-bit target; a slice of at least 4 GiB in a single call.
finding.sink: ptr::copy_nonoverlapping writing input.len() bytes into self.mem ([u32; 4], 16 bytes) via Buffer::copy_from_slice (src/utils.rs:44-48).

trace.note: Write::write forwards the full buf to update with no size cap.
total_len wrapping_add with input.len() as u32; truncation harmless (hash only).
(mem_size + input.len() as u32) < 16 uses truncated length; passes when len = 2^32 + k, k < 16.
Buffer::copy_from_slice(input) with the full, untruncated input.
Only bounds check is debug_assert; absent in release builds.
ptr::copy_nonoverlapping copies the full length into the 16-byte mem buffer, overflowing the hasher struct.
mem_size += input.len() as u32 (also truncated); state corruption follows.

finding.guards_checked: Only debug_assert at src/utils.rs:45 (release-disabled); no length cap in update or Write impl; the u32 cast at xxh32.rs:104 only sets is_large_len. Safe counterpart: Xxh64::update (src/xxh64.rs:119) uses usize arithmetic. Not executed: no shell tool available to build or run a reproducer.
